Posterior predictive distribution for a new site

Source: R/predict.R
predict.bef_fit_re.Rd

Draws from the posterior predictive distribution for a site that was not in the data: either its true effect, or the estimate that a new study with a given standard error would produce. For a new site whose estimate is already known, predict() instead returns the mean, standard deviation, interval and mode of the posterior distribution of its effect.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'bef_fit_re'
predict(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  ...,
  type = c("theta", "theta_hat"),
  n = NULL,
  jitter = FALSE,
  seed = NULL,
  level = 0.9
)

Arguments

object

A bef_fit object created by bayes_efron_fit().

newdata

For type = "theta_hat", a numeric vector of positive standard errors, one per new site. It is required for that type and not used for type = "theta". Can also be a data frame with the columns estimate and se, for new sites whose estimates are known; see Details.

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

type

Quantity to draw for a new site: "theta" (the default) for its true effect, or "theta_hat" for its estimate.

n

Number of draws, a positive integer. If NULL (the default), the number of posterior draws in the fit is used. If n is larger than that, posterior draws of \(g\) are used more than once.

jitter

If TRUE, the draws from a fit with point masses are spread between the grid points; see Details.

seed

Integer seed for the draws. If NULL (the default), no seed is set. If a seed is specified, the state of R's random number generator is restored afterward.

level

Posterior probability of the interval in the columns lower and upper, a number between 0 and 1. Only used if newdata is a data frame.

Value

For type = "theta", and for type = "theta_hat" with one standard error in newdata, a numeric vector of n draws. For type = "theta_hat" with more than one standard error, a matrix with n rows and one column per standard error.

If newdata is a data frame, a data frame with one row per row of newdata and the following columns.

estimate, se

The estimate and its standard error, as given.

mean, sd

The posterior mean and the posterior standard deviation of the effect.

lower, upper

The limits of the posterior interval at level.

mode

The posterior mode.

Details

predict() has three uses, which are selected by type and newdata.

  • type = "theta" (the default) draws the true effect of a new site from \(g\). Each draw uses a different posterior draw of \(g\), so the draws describe the distribution of effects and include the uncertainty about \(g\).

  • type = "theta_hat" draws the estimate that a new study would produce: sampling error with the standard error given in newdata is added to a draw of the effect. If newdata contains several standard errors, the result has one column per new site. Each row then uses one posterior draw of \(g\) for all sites and draws a separate effect and sampling error for each site, so the sites in a row are independent given that draw.

  • If newdata is a data frame with the columns estimate and se, the estimates of the new sites are known. Nothing is drawn, and for each row predict() returns the posterior mean, the posterior standard deviation, the interval at level and the posterior mode of the effect. type, n, jitter and seed are not used.

For a fit with point masses, \(g\) is a distribution on the grid, so each draw of an effect is one of the grid points. If jitter = TRUE, a uniform random number between minus and plus half the grid spacing is added to the draw, which spreads the draws over the intervals between the grid points. For a fit with component = "normal", a draw comes from the normal component at the grid point that was drawn, and jitter is not used.

A new site with a known estimate was not in the data, so before its estimate is observed the distribution of its effect is the posterior mean of \(g\). Bayes' rule with the estimate then gives the posterior distribution that predict() summarizes. The summaries are those that the site would have in a fit of the data with that site added, on the same grid, up to Monte Carlo error. They differ from the summaries that site_summary() gives for a site in the fit with the same estimate and standard error, because that site's estimate was already used to estimate \(g\). The difference is small when there are many sites and is largest for an estimate in a tail of the distribution. Each row of newdata is treated as the only new site, so the other rows do not affect its result. For a fit with point masses, the interval limits are computed as in site_summary() with its default reading.

See also

site_summary(), bef_fit, bayes_efron_fit()

Examples

# The callback gap of a firm that was not in the data.
theta_new <- predict(krw_fit, seed = 1)
quantile(theta_new, c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95))
#>           5%          50%          95% 
#> -0.008055305  0.013672701  0.045057598 
mean(theta_new > 0)
#> [1] 0.85625

# An estimate with a standard error of 1 percentage point.
estimate_new <- predict(krw_fit, newdata = 0.01, type = "theta_hat",
                        seed = 1)
quantile(estimate_new, c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95))
#>          5%         50%         95% 
#> -0.01264502  0.01529825  0.04897299 

# Two new firms whose estimates are known: gaps of 0 and of 5 percentage
# points, with standard errors of 1 and 2 points.
predict(krw_fit, newdata = data.frame(estimate = c(0, 0.05),
                                      se = c(0.01, 0.02)))
#>   estimate   se        mean          sd        lower      upper        mode
#> 1     0.00 0.01 0.005452166 0.007714249 -0.007174759 0.01826861 0.006430032
#> 2     0.05 0.02 0.028766853 0.014235719  0.007674624 0.05445411 0.025743815
